title: Not close, apparently
setting: A weeknight at home. Okaasan hasn't heard from Yuki for a week and is starting to worry; Kenji is slumped on the sofa with his phone.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.ja: ケンジ、ユキから連絡来た？
lines.kana: けんじ、ゆきかられんらくきた？
lines.english: Kenji, have you heard from Yuki?

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: e, kenji ni wa renraku kuru no? okaasan ni wa senshuu kara konai no yo.
lines.ja: え、ケンジには連絡来るの？お母さんには先週から来ないのよ。
lines.kana: え、けんじにはれんらくくるの？おかあさんにはせんしゅうからこないのよ。
lines.english: Wait, she gets in touch with you? I haven't heard a thing from her since last week.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.ja: 仕事忙しいんじゃない？
lines.kana: しごといそがしいんじゃない？
lines.english: Maybe she's just busy with work?

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: demo, denwa shite mo denai shi, renraku torenai no yo.
lines.ja: でも、電話しても出ないし、連絡取れないのよ。
lines.kana: でも、でんわしてもでないし、れんらくとれないのよ。
lines.english: But she doesn't pick up when I call. I just can't get hold of her.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: ore ni wa mainichi renraku kuru kedo.
lines.ja: 俺には毎日連絡来るけど。
lines.kana: おれにはまいにちれんらくくるけど。
lines.english: Well, I hear from her every day.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: mainichi renraku totteru no? itsu kara sonna ni naka ii no?
lines.ja: 毎日連絡取ってるの？いつからそんなに仲いいの？
lines.kana: まいにちれんらくとってるの？いつからそんなになかいいの？
lines.english: You two are in touch every day? Since when are you so close?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: betsu ni naka yokunai yo. geemu no hanashi bakkari da shi.
lines.ja: 別に仲良くないよ。ゲームの話ばっかりだし。
lines.kana: べつになかよくないよ。げーむのはなしばっかりだし。
lines.english: We're not close or anything. It's all just game stuff.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: sou? mukashi wa sugoku naka warukatta noni ne.
lines.ja: そう？昔はすごく仲悪かったのにね。
lines.kana: そう？むかしはすごくなかわるかったのにね。
lines.english: Oh, really? You two used to get on so badly, too.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: jaa, okaasan ga yuki to naka waruku natta n ja nai?
lines.ja: じゃあ、お母さんがユキと仲悪くなったんじゃない？
lines.kana: じゃあ、おかあさんがゆきとなかわるくなったんじゃない？
lines.english: So maybe it's you she's fallen out with.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: naka warukunai wa yo! senshuu mo futari de kaimono ni itta no yo.
lines.ja: 仲悪くないわよ！先週も二人で買い物に行ったのよ。
lines.kana: なかわるくないわよ！せんしゅうもふたりでかいものにいったのよ。
lines.english: We are not on bad terms! We went shopping together just last week.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.kana: あ！ゆきかられんらくきた！
lines.english: Oh! It's a message from Yuki!

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: shigoto isogashikute gomen tte. shuumatsu kaeru tte!
lines.ja: 仕事忙しくてごめんって。週末帰るって！
lines.kana: しごといそがしくてごめんって。しゅうまつかえるって！
lines.english: She says sorry, work's been busy. And she's coming home this weekend!

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.ja: よかったね、連絡取れて。
lines.kana: よかったね、れんらくとれて。
lines.english: Good, so you got hold of her.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: ato, kenji to geemu shitai tte. yappari naka ii n ja nai.
lines.ja: あと、ケンジとゲームしたいって。やっぱり仲いいんじゃない。
lines.kana: あと、けんじとげーむしたいって。やっぱりなかいいんじゃない。
lines.english: And she wants to play games with you. See, you two do get along.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.ja: だから、仲良くないって。
lines.kana: だから、なかよくないって。
lines.english: Like I said, we're not close.

choices.english: Kenji and Yuki have fallen out, so Okaasan tells Kenji to call his sister and make up before the weekend.
Okaasan can't get hold of Yuki, so Kenji phones her; Yuki picks up and says she'll go shopping with Okaasan at the weekend.
Okaasan hasn't heard from Yuki since last week, though Kenji hears from her every day. Then Yuki messages: work's been busy, and she's coming home this weekend.

questions.explanation: Lines 1-6: Okaasan has heard nothing since last week and can't reach Yuki (line 3: okaasan ni wa senshuu kara konai no yo; line 5: renraku torenai no yo), but Kenji hears from her every day (line 6: ore ni wa mainichi renraku kuru kedo). Lines 13-15: a message arrives (a! yuki kara renraku kita!): sorry, work's been busy, and she's coming home at the weekend (shuumatsu kaeru tte). A is wrong: Kenji and Yuki only got on badly in the old days (line 9: mukashi wa), they're in touch every day now, and nobody is told to call anyone. B is wrong: nobody phones Yuki in the scene; she messages Okaasan herself, and the shopping trip was last week (line 11: senshuu mo futari de kaimono ni itta no yo).

questions.english: Sora asks you, "ne, kenta to yuki-san tte, mukashi kara no tomodachi na n da tte?" (Hey, I hear Kenta and Yuki have been friends for ages?) They have, and they still get on really well. Tell him they're close.
questions.ja: ね、ケンタとユキさんって、昔からの友達なんだって？
questions.kana: ね、けんたとゆきさんって、むかしからのともだちなんだって？
questions.romaji: ne, kenta to yuki-san tte, mukashi kara no tomodachi na n da tte?
questions.answer: Say their relationship is good with naka ga ii (ga can drop in speech): un, ano futari, sugoku naka ii yo.

modelAnswers.romaji: un, ano futari, sugoku naka ii yo.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、あの二人、すごく仲いいよ。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, those two are really close.

modelAnswers.romaji: hai, ano futari wa sugoku naka ga ii n desu yo.
modelAnswers.ja: はい、あの二人はすごく仲がいいんですよ。
modelAnswers.english: Yes, those two get on really well.

questions.explanation: English 'get along' sends you looking for a verb, but Japanese says the relationship (naka) is good: naka ga ii. Okaasan asks it in line 7 (itsu kara sonna ni naka ii no?) and says it again in line 17 (yappari naka ii n ja nai). Kenji's denial in lines 8 and 18 is the negative, naka yokunai: ii turns into yo- when it changes form. nakayoku suru is the action, being nice to each other (nakayoku shite ne), so it doesn't describe how two people get on. And 'close' here is not chikai, which is near in distance. The second model is the polite version, for someone like Tanaka-san.

questions.english: Kenji teases his mother: "jaa, okaasan ga yuki to naka waruku natta n ja nai?" What is he suggesting?
questions.ja: ケンジさんは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: けんじさんはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: kenji-san wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: That Okaasan has been feeling unwell, so Yuki is leaving her to rest.
That Okaasan and Yuki have fallen out, and that's why Yuki isn't getting in touch.
That Okaasan has been in a bad mood lately, so Yuki doesn't feel like calling her.

questions.explanation: Line 10: naka ga warui is about how two people get on (yuki to = with Yuki), and waruku natta means it has become bad: they've fallen out. Kenji is joking that this, not work, is why Yuki has gone quiet, and Okaasan protests in line 11 (naka warukunai wa yo!) that the two of them went shopping just last week. A would be guai ga warui (feeling unwell) and C kigen ga warui (in a bad mood): both describe one person, and neither has naka. Okaasan used the same phrase about the past in line 9: mukashi wa sugoku naka warukatta, Kenji and Yuki used to get on badly.

questions.english: Okaasan asks you, "yuki wa shuumatsu nanji ni kaeru no? kiite kureta?" (What time is Yuki getting home this weekend? Did you ask her?) You've called her several times, but she isn't picking up. Tell your mother you can't get hold of her.
questions.ja: ユキは週末何時に帰るの？聞いてくれた？
questions.kana: ゆきはしゅうまつなんじにかえるの？きいてくれた？
questions.romaji: yuki wa shuumatsu nanji ni kaeru no? kiite kureta?
questions.answer: Say you can't reach her with the can-form of toru: renraku torenai n da.

modelAnswers.romaji: nando mo denwa shita kedo, renraku torenai n da.
modelAnswers.ja: 何度も電話したけど、連絡取れないんだ。
modelAnswers.english: I've called her loads of times, but I can't get hold of her.

modelAnswers.romaji: uun, mada renraku torenai yo. denwa shite mo denai n da.
modelAnswers.ja: ううん、まだ連絡取れないよ。電話しても出ないんだ。
modelAnswers.english: No, I still can't reach her. She doesn't pick up.

questions.explanation: Getting through to someone, or staying in touch with them over time, is renraku o toru. Here it's the can-form torenai, 'I can't get hold of her', just as Okaasan says in line 5 (denwa shite mo denai shi, renraku torenai no yo). Okaasan uses the ongoing form in line 7 (mainichi renraku totteru no? = you're in touch every day?), and Kenji the positive in line 16 when the message finally comes (yokatta ne, renraku torete). English 'contact her' or 'keep in touch' points to renraku suru, but that is sending one message or making one call (mata renraku suru ne): renraku shita only says you sent something, not that you couldn't reach her.

questions.english: Right at the start, Okaasan asks Kenji about his sister. What did she ask?
questions.ja: お母さんは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: おかあさんはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: okaasan wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: Kenji, have you heard from Yuki?
Kenji, did Yuki tell you (about it)?
Kenji, did you get in touch with Yuki?

questions.explanation: Line 1: renraku ga kuru (ga dropped, past kita) is a message or call coming to you, with the sender marked by kara: yuki kara renraku kita? = have you heard from Yuki? Kenji answers with the same verb in line 2 (un, kesa kita kedo), and Okaasan uses it again in line 3 (okaasan ni wa senshuu kara konai no yo) and line 13 when the message arrives (a! yuki kara renraku kita!). B is English 'hear from' put into Japanese: yuki kara kiita means being told something by Yuki, a piece of news, not getting a message from her. C turns it round: renraku shita? asks whether Kenji contacted Yuki, but Okaasan wants to know whether Yuki has been in touch, which is why Kenji's answer is kita, not shita.

newWords.english: phone call; denwa suru = call (denwa shite mo denai = she doesn't pick up when I call)
I, me (casual, mostly men and boys)
not particularly (betsu ni naka yokunai = we're not close or anything)
the old days, back then (mukashi wa = used to)
two people, the two of them (futari de = the two of us together)
just as I thought; after all
